lesson_scope: Evaluating composite ranges, solving composite equations with domain rejection, inverting composite functions, composite of inverse, and geometric intersection via discriminant.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: determining the range of a composite function with quadratic inner component.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding range of composite linear-quadratic function.

hints: First determine the range of the inner function $g(x) = x^2 + 5$: since $x^2 \ge 0$, $g(x) \ge 5$.
Because $f(u) = 3u + 2$ is strictly increasing, evaluate $f$ at the minimum inner output $u = 5$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the output range of the inner function $g(x) = x^2 + 5$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$\text{For all } x \in \mathbb{R}, \ x^2 \ge 0 \implies g(x) = x^2 + 5 \ge 5$$
$$\text{Range of } g: \quad g(x) \ge 5$$

Apply the outer increasing linear function $f(u) = 3u + 2$ to $u \ge 5$:
$$\text{Minimum of } fg: \quad f(5) = 3(5) + 2 = 17$$
$$\text{Range of } fg: \quad fg(x) \ge 17$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds the range of the inner function $g$ as $g(x) \ge 5$.
Evaluates $f(5) = 3(5) + 2 = 17$ and states the range of $fg$ as $fg(x) \ge 17$ (or $y \ge 17$ or $[17, \infty)$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving a linear composite equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving a linear composite equation.

walkthrough.text:
Form the composite expression $fg(x)$:
$$fg(x) = 4(5 - 2x) - 1 = 20 - 8x - 1 = 19 - 8x$$

Set the linear expression equal to $11$ and solve:
$$19 - 8x = 11 \implies 8x = 8 \implies x = 1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving an inverse composite equation via direct function evaluation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving f^-1(g(x)) = k by transforming to g(x) = f(k).

walkthrough.text:
Apply the outer function $f$ to both sides of the equation:
$$f^{-1}(g(x)) = 4 \iff g(x) = f(4)$$

Compute $f(4)$ and solve for $x$:
$$f(4) = 2(4) + 9 = 17$$
$$g(x) = 17 \implies 3x - 1 = 17 \implies 3x = 18 \implies x = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $f$ to both sides to obtain $g(x) = f(4) = 2(4) + 9 = 17$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying composite inverse reversal law (gf)^-1 = f^-1 g^-1.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the inverse composite reversal rule.

hints: Remember the socks-and-shoes rule for composite inverses: $(gf)^{-1}(x) \equiv f^{-1}(g^{-1}(x))$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the reversal law for the inverse of a composite function:
$$(gf)^{-1}(x) \equiv f^{-1}(g^{-1}(x))$$

Substitute $g^{-1}(x) = 5x - 1$ into $f^{-1}(u) = \dfrac{u + 3}{2}$ and simplify:
$$(gf)^{-1}(x) = \frac{(5x - 1) + 3}{2} = \frac{5x + 2}{2} = \frac{5}{2}x + 1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving composite equation with domain rejection for quadratic term.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving quadratic composite and discarding out-of-domain root.

hints: Find $x = 2$ or $x = -3$, and discard $x = -3$ because the domain specifies $x \ge 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up and solve the composite equation:
$$fg(x) = (2x + 1)^2 - 7 = 18 \implies (2x + 1)^2 = 25$$
$$2x + 1 = 5 \implies 2x = 4 \implies x = 2$$
$$2x + 1 = -5 \implies 2x = -6 \implies x = -3$$

Check the domain restriction of the inner function $g$, which is $x \ge 0$:
$$\text{Since } x \ge 0, \text{ we reject } x = -3$$
$$\text{The unique valid solution is } x = 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves $2x + 1 = 5 \implies x = 2$ and rejects $x = -3$ due to the domain condition $x \ge 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: evaluating composite of an inverse function at a numerical point.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of nested inverse evaluation.

hints: First find the input that produces $7$ in $f$: solve $3x - 5 = 7$.

walkthrough.text:
Find $f^{-1}(7)$ by solving $f(x) = 7$:
$$3x - 5 = 7 \implies 3x = 12 \implies f^{-1}(7) = 4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: forming a linear-quadratic composite in completed square form, determining its range, and solving a quadratic value equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expressing a composite function in completed square form.

walkthrough.text:
Complete the square for the inner function $g(x)$:
$$g(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7 = (x - 2)^2 - 4 + 7 = (x - 2)^2 + 3$$

Substitute into the linear outer function $f$:
$$fg(x) = f(g(x)) = 2\left[(x - 2)^2 + 3\right] - 3 = 2(x - 2)^2 + 6 - 3 = 2(x - 2)^2 + 3$$
Thus, $A = 2, B = 2, C = 3$.

ai_rubric.observable: Completes the square on $g(x)$ to get $(x - 2)^2 + 3$ and substitutes into $f$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the range and solving an equation for a composite quadratic.

hints: From $fg(x) = 2(x - 2)^2 + 3$, the minimum value is $3$, so the range is $fg(x) \ge 3$.
Take the square root: $x - 2 = \pm 3$, giving $x = 5$ and $x = -1$.

walkthrough.text:
State the range from the completed square form:
Because $2(x - 2)^2 \ge 0$, the minimum value is $3$, so:
$$\text{Range of } fg: \quad fg(x) \ge 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: forming a self-composite ff(x) to solve a linear value equation, and inverting g to solve g^-1(f(x)) = 1.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming self-composite and solving a linear equation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $f(x)$ into itself to obtain $ff(x)$:
$$ff(x) = 4 - 3(4 - 3x) = 4 - 12 + 9x = 9x - 8$$

Solve the linear equation $ff(x) = 25$:
$$9x - 8 = 25$$
$$9x = 33 \implies x = \dfrac{33}{9} = \dfrac{11}{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving an equation involving the composite of an inverse function.

walkthrough.text:
Find the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$:
$$y = 2x + 5 \implies x = \dfrac{y - 5}{2} \implies g^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - 5}{2}$$

Substitute $f(x) = 4 - 3x$ into $g^{-1}$ and solve:
$$\dfrac{4 - 3x - 5}{2} = 1$$
$$-3x - 1 = 2$$
$$-3x = 3 \implies x = -1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: forming composite of inverse with quadratic inner function and solving a quadratic equation to find exact roots in surd form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the composite of an inverse function with a quadratic function.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$:
$$y = 3x + 1 \implies 3x = y - 1 \implies g^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - 1}{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving a quadratic equation in exact surd form.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the expression to zero and simplify:
$$\dfrac{2x^2 + 8x - 4}{3} = 0$$
$$2x^2 + 8x - 4 = 0$$
$$x^2 + 4x - 2 = 0$$

Solve using completing the square:
$$(x + 2)^2 - 4 - 2 = 0$$
$$(x + 2)^2 = 6$$
$$x = -2 \pm \sqrt{6}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $2x^2 + 8x - 4 = 0 \implies x^2 + 4x - 2 = 0$ and applies quadratic formula / CTS.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: forming a rational-linear composite function and solving a quadratic value equation with domain rejection of extraneous root.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming a rational composite function.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $g(x)$ into $f(x)$:
$$fg(x) = \dfrac{12}{(3x - 1)^2 - 4}$$

Expand and simplify the denominator:
$$(3x - 1)^2 - 4 = 9x^2 - 6x + 1 - 4 = 9x^2 - 6x - 3 = 3(3x^2 - 2x - 1)$$
$$fg(x) = \dfrac{12}{3(3x^2 - 2x - 1)} = \dfrac{4}{3x^2 - 2x - 1}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving an equation involving a rational composite with domain restriction rejection.

hints: Domain of $g$ requires $x > 1$. Show that $\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{19}}{3} < 1$ is rejected, leaving $x = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{19}}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the composite expression to $\dfrac{4}{5}$ and cross-multiply:
$$\dfrac{12}{(3x - 1)^2 - 4} = \dfrac{4}{5}$$
$$4\left[(3x - 1)^2 - 4\right] = 60$$
$$(3x - 1)^2 - 4 = 15$$
$$(3x - 1)^2 = 19$$

Solve for $x$:
$$3x - 1 = \pm\sqrt{19} \implies x = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{19}}{3}$$

Check against the composite input domain $x > 1$:
- $x = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{19}}{3} \approx \dfrac{1 + 4.359}{3} = 1.786 > 1$ (valid).
- $x = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{19}}{3} \approx \dfrac{1 - 4.359}{3} = -1.120 < 1$ (rejected).
$$\text{Solution: } x = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{19}}{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: forming a linear composite gf, inverting the composite, and proving the reversal identity (gf)^-1 = f^-1 g^-1.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming a composite of two linear functions.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $f(x) = 2x + 7$ into the outer function $g(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}x - 4$:
$$gf(x) = g(f(x)) = \dfrac{1}{3}(2x + 7) - 4$$

Simplify by combining terms over a common denominator:
$$gf(x) = \dfrac{2x + 7}{3} - \dfrac{12}{3} = \dfrac{2x - 5}{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Inverting a composite function and showing identity with reverse composition of inverses.

walkthrough.text:
Find the inverse of the composite function $gf(x)$:
$$y = \dfrac{2x - 5}{3} \implies 3y = 2x - 5 \implies x = \dfrac{3y + 5}{2}$$
$$(gf)^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3x + 5}{2}$$

Find the individual inverses $f^{-1}(x)$ and $g^{-1}(x)$:
$$g(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}x - 4 \implies g^{-1}(x) = 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12$$
$$f(x) = 2x + 7 \implies f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - 7}{2}$$

Compose the individual inverses in reverse order:
$$f^{-1}(g^{-1}(x)) = f^{-1}(3x + 12) = \dfrac{(3x + 12) - 7}{2} = \dfrac{3x + 5}{2}$$
This confirms $(gf)^{-1}(x) \equiv f^{-1}(g^{-1}(x))$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: setting up composite-inverse equation g^-1(f(x)) = g(x) with parameter k and applying the discriminant tangency condition D = 0 to solve k and point of contact P.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming expressions for an inverse and composite of an inverse containing a parameter.

hints: Invert $y = 3x + k \implies x = \dfrac{y - k}{3} \implies g^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - k}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine $g^{-1}(x)$ in terms of $k$:
$$y = 3x + k \implies 3x = y - k \implies g^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - k}{3}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding parameter and point of contact using discriminant tangency condition.

hints: For tangency (single point of contact), set $b^2 - 4ac = 0$: $(-4)^2 - 4(2)(3 - 4k) = 0 \implies 16 - 24 + 32k = 0 \implies k = 1/4$.
Substitute $k = 1/4$ back into the quadratic: $2x^2 - 4x + 2 = 0 \implies 2(x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = 1, y = 3(1) + 1/4 = 13/4$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the two functions and rearrange to standard quadratic form:
$$\dfrac{2x^2 + 5x + 3 - k}{3} = 3x + k$$
$$2x^2 + 5x + 3 - k = 9x + 3k$$
$$2x^2 - 4x + (3 - 4k) = 0$$

Find the coordinates of the point of contact $P$:
Substitute $k = \dfrac{1}{4}$ into the quadratic equation:
$$2x^2 - 4x + 2 = 0 \implies 2(x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = 1$$
$$y = g(1) = 3(1) + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{13}{4}$$
$$P = \left(1, \dfrac{13}{4}\right)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: domain-range existence proof for a trigonometric composite function, finding exact composite range, and solving a trigonometric value equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving that a trigonometric composite function is defined via domain-range subset condition.

hints: Evaluate $g(x) = 2x$ on $0 \le x \le \pi/2$: as $x$ ranges from $0$ to $\pi/2$, $2x$ ranges from $0$ to $\pi$.
Compare with domain of $f$ ($[0, \pi]$) and conclude that $\text{Range}(g) \subseteq \text{Domain}(f)$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the range of the inner function $g$ on $0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$g(0) = 2(0) = 0$$
$$g\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi$$
$$\text{Range of } g: \quad [0, \pi]$$

Compare with the domain of the outer function $f$:
$$\text{Domain of } f: \quad [0, \pi]$$
Because $\text{Range}(g) = [0, \pi] \subseteq \text{Domain}(f) = [0, \pi]$, every output of $g$ is a valid input for $f$.
Therefore, the composite function $fg$ is defined for all $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates range of $g$ as $0 \le g(x) \le \pi$ on $[0, \pi/2]$.
Compares range of $g$ with domain of $f$ ($[0, \pi]$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the range of a trigonometric composite function.

hints: As $x \in [0, \pi/2]$, the angle $2x \in [0, \pi]$, so $\cos(2x)$ takes all values from $1$ down to $-1$.
Compute minimum: $5 - 6(1) = -1$; maximum: $5 - 6(-1) = 11$. Range is $-1 \le fg(x) \le 11$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the composite function expression:
$$fg(x) = f(2x) = 5 - 6\cos(2x)$$

Determine the range of $fg$ over the angle interval $2x \in [0, \pi]$:
$$\text{Minimum: } 5 - 6(1) = -1 \quad (\text{at } 2x = 0)$$
$$\text{Maximum: } 5 - 6(-1) = 11 \quad (\text{at } 2x = \pi)$$
$$\text{Range of } fg: \quad -1 \le fg(x) \le 11$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving a trigonometric composite equation.

hints: In the interval $2x \in [0, \pi]$, the only solution is $2x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the equation to isolate $\cos(2x)$:
$$5 - 6\cos(2x) = 2$$
$$6\cos(2x) = 3$$
$$\cos(2x) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Find the angle in $[0, \pi]$ and solve for $x$:
$$2x = \arccos\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$$
$$x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$$
Since $\dfrac{\pi}{6} \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, it is the unique valid solution.
